newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Trygg-Hansa H1 seen tied to equity gains.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Trygg-Hansa H1 seen tied to equity gains.

text.p: Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa on Tuesday posted slightly higher than expected first half 1997 profits but analysts said the result was largely dependent on the strong Swedish stock market.
Trygg-Hansa pre-tax profits rose 42 percent to 2.13 billion crowns ($265.9 million) against market expectations of a pre-tax profit of 1.94 billion crowns.
The insurer's share price fell on the report, losing seven crowns to 167, partly due to a strong run ahead of the report and partly due to some fears of overdependency on equity moves.
"People are starting to say what will happen next year if there is not the same strong equity market," said Goldman Sachs analyst Giovanni Govi.
Trygg-Hansa's chief executive Lars Thunell attributed the higher profits partly to a very strong investment return.

"Our successful venture in the expanding life insurance and savings market continues and the strong investment returns have contributed to further improvement in Trygg-Hansa's financial strength," Thunell said in a statement.

The combined value of investments in the company's asset management rose to 153 billion crowns at the half year mark from 127 billion a year ago. Its combined net ratio rose to 110 percent from 109 percent.
Shareholders' funds on June 30 amounted to 11.34 billion crowns against 8.18 billion a year ago which corresponded to 137 crowns a share versus 99 crowns.
But analysts also welcomed a sharp increase in volumes in the life and savings market as a positive sign.

Trygg-Hansa said its portfolio of life insurance and savings business increased by 15 percent to 134.61 billion crowns in the first six months with a combined result of 163 million crowns compared to 25 million a year ago.
"The underlying insurance operations look to be heading for a better second half," said one Stockholm-based analyst.
He said cost cutting initiated by the company had not yet filtered onto the balance sheet and this should also start to have some impact on the second half.
"Overall it was a good report but it gave no indication of what will happen if the sharemarket starts to tail off," he said.

Trygg-Hansa's non-life operations were disappointing, showing no signs of coming out of stagnation, with continued strong rate pressure and premium volumes continuing to decline, primarily for commerical insurance.
The balance on the technical account for non-life insurance business fell to 170 million crowns from 367 million crowns a year ago.
But despite some reservations, analysts were generally positive about the company's performance.
"The company is doing well with some of this is due to external acquisitions," said Govi, referring particularly to the February acquisition of Credit Lyonnais' Swedish bank operations.
"The life and savings performance was very good but this is still only a small business in Trygg-Hansa. It still has quite a way to go yet."
Trygg-Hansa said a 2.0 billion crowns redemption of 13.14 million B-series shares, that was decided in May, was expected to be completed sometime around September 24 this year.
-- Stockholm newsroom +6-8-700 1017 ($ = 8.01 Swedish Crowns)
